audience: the person everybody in the group asks what happens next (listing audience[0])
parents packing for children or a baby, one list per child
people planning a first trip abroad and checking passports, entry rules and paper copies
multi-stop travellers whose flights, transfers, stays and reservations were booked around each other
people who have lived through a delay cascade and now save 'what to do if your flight is delayed' pins
people who want a paper copy for when the phone is at four percent in a taxi
road trippers and carry-on-only packers who save packing checklists

visualWorld.setting: The travel desk and the departure hall, seen from above or straight on: an open suitcase on a floor, a passport and its paperwork laid out in a travel folder, a departure board over a gate, boarding passes and luggage tags, a printed itinerary on a clipboard, a route drawn across a simple map. Everything is the stuff a traveller actually handles, drawn flat. No people's faces, no destinations' landmarks, no photos.

props.draw: Top-down open hard-shell case: two rounded rects side by side (lid and base) joined by a zip seam drawn as a dashed line; soft lining fill; two thin crossed elastic straps in the base; a rounded bar handle on the outer edge; four small circle wheels at the corners.
Upright cabin trolley: tall rounded rect body, front pocket as an inner rounded rect with a zip line, telescopic handle as two thin vertical rects plus a crossbar, two circle wheels.

Knolled small items, each 3-6 shapes: folded clothes (stacked rounded rects with a fold line), socks (two L shapes), shoes (two sole shapes with a heel notch), toothbrush (thin rect + small bristle block), medication bottle (rect, cap rect, blank label band), bank card (rounded rect + chip square), cash (rect with an oval), phone (rounded rect, dark screen), charger (plug block + looping cable path), power bank (rounded rect + four LED dots), sunglasses (two circles + bridge), sun hat (ellipse brim + dome), folded copies (rect with a corner fold). Laid on a grid with even gaps, all axis-aligned.
Quart zip bag: translucent rounded rect (low-opacity fill, solid outline), zip strip as a thicker band on top, three small bottles inside (rect + cap).

Baby bottle (rect, teat as a dome), nappy (rounded trapezoid with tab rects), comfort toy (bear silhouette: circle head, two ear circles, rounded body), small water bottle, picture book (two rects with a spine line).

Closed: portrait rounded rect (about 0.7 ratio) in the strong accent, a foil emblem as a plain circle-and-ring, no country, no crest, no lettering. Open: two pages, the photo page as a square photo placeholder (silhouette circle + shoulders) and two rows of short dashes for the machine-readable lines, no characters.
Open document wallet: two panels side by side with pocket flaps (trapezoids), an elastic band as a thin vertical strip, and coloured index tabs along the top edge that can carry real labels.
Envelope (rect + triangular flap line) with a folded sheet sliding out; the sheet shows a header bar and one bold line that carries a real booking reference.
Bifold wallet rounded rect with a stitch line, two card edges peeking out, a banknote corner with an oval.

Wide rounded rect; perforation as a dashed vertical line with two semicircle notches cut from top and bottom edges; stub on the right; barcode as 20-30 vertical bars of varying width (decorative, no digits); a small plane glyph between two large fields; label/value grid in small caps. Labels and values must be real words from the pin's source, never airline codes or invented gates and seats.

Tag shape: rounded rect with the two top corners chamfered, a reinforced eyelet (two concentric circles), a string loop drawn as a single curved stroke; kraft or coral fill; one writing area with a ruled line. Carries one real item per tag.
Card-ratio rounded rect with a magnetic stripe band or a small chip square, tucked half into a paper sleeve (rect with a diagonal flap). Carries one real line each.
Half-circle dome on a flat ellipse base, a small knob on top, two short motion lines.

Dark rounded panel with a slim frame; a header row of column labels in small caps; rows of split-flap cells (each character in its own small rect with a hairline across the middle, slight gap between cells); an optional status column of pill-shaped flaps; a small round clock top left. Rows are the pin's real lines.
Circle, 12 tick marks, two hands; when several clocks sit together their hands show real relative offsets for one chosen instant, or are drawn without hands.

Pale map ground with two or three loose land blobs (no real coastline, no country names), a dashed bezier arc between round teardrop location pins, a tiny plane or train glyph riding the line; each pin can carry a small card with a real stop name and booking.
Winding road ribbon with a dashed centre line, side-view flat car (body rect, window rects, two wheel circles), small stop markers: fuel drop, cabin (pentagon roof + door), house.
Small booking cards connected top to bottom by a thick line with arrowheads, each card a rounded rect with a kind label in small caps; an 'affected' card gets a dashed outline, never a red alarm.
Simple figures: head circle and rounded-shoulder body, no faces, 3-6 in different tints; used beside a booking card, never as portraits.

Portrait white sheet with a soft drop shadow and one curled corner (triangle); header eyebrow and title; rows with square tick boxes; a ticked row gets a check and a strike line (the PDF really prints ticked items struck through).
Stack of 4-6 offset sheets with a staple or spiral (row of small circles) on the left; top page titled with the real book title; coloured side tabs carrying real section names.
Board rect with rounded corners and a clip (small rounded rect + semicircle) at the top centre holding a printed sheet.
Landscape card, red top rule and pale blue ruled lines, slightly rotated, holding a short real wording.

Landscape card split by a vertical rule: message area left, three address lines right (blank), stamp as a rect with a scalloped border (circles along the edge) and wavy postmark strokes with no lettering.
Square with a folded bottom-right corner, tilted 3-5 degrees, holding one short real line.
Long thin rect with a tapered tip triangle and a clip strip.
Rounded phone frame with a thin bezel and pill notch, the real screenshot from creative/public/screens/ clipped inside, cropped to the part the pin talks about; never redrawn or edited.
Phone face-up with a dark blank screen and a large battery glyph (rounded rect + nub) with only a thin sliver of fill; no app UI, no notification.

visualWorld.palette: Start from the product's own accent in src/products/travel-companion/definition.ts (base #00626f, strong #00434d, soft #d9eef0, page #eef4f5): the teal is the 'airline livery' colour for passports, board frames, route lines and pins. Add the materials of travel as neutrals: kraft/manila for tags and folders, warm white for boarding passes and paper, a near-black teal for the departure board with warm amber flap letters, and one warm coral pop (the soft coral of the time chips in the itinerary screenshot) for luggage tags and the single highlighted item. Never more than one pop colour per pin; the teal stays recognisably this product's.
visualWorld.mood: Calm competence at the airport: the feeling of having the reference ready before the desk asks. Orderly, tactile, a little nostalgic in the paper objects, never frantic, never glossy-luxury, never wanderlust. The tone of the listing: practical, quiet, nothing promised that the app does not do.

archetypes.name: Packing flat-lay
archetypes.clicks: Packing lists are the most reliable traffic driver in travel Pinterest (Simple Pin Media); Pinterest reported 'packing guide' searches up 480% year over year (via Social Media Today), and travellers say they use Pinterest to decide what to pack (Skift, citing Deep Focus). The knolled top-down flat-lay is the dominant look of packing pins: the eye scans it like a checklist, so it reads as useful and gets saved for later.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Top 0-330: headline block on the page colour, left-aligned at x=64, max 3 lines; eyebrow above it if the title has a 'Keyword:' prefix. 330-1180: top-down open suitcase (or carry-on, or a grid of small bags) filling the width with 48px margins; 6-15 knolled items on an even grid, each with a small label in a kraft label strip beneath it. 1180-1330: the sub line, one or two lines. 1330-1500: product line 'Travel Companion' + small mark at bottom-left (keep the bottom-right corner empty for Pinterest's icons).
archetypes.visual: open-suitcase or carry-on-bag seen from above, the real items knolled around or inside it, a clear liquids bag where relevant, sometimes split into two zones (shared / personal).
archetypes.text: Headline = the pin's title. Item labels = the real items, copied exactly from STARTER_LISTS in src/products/travel-companion/packingLists.ts or the matching packing guide in src/content/guides.ts. Zone labels only where the source has them ('Shared, packed once' / 'Personal, one each'; group names like 'Documents and money').
archetypes.bestFor: packing list pins: week away, carry-on only, the basics, kids and baby, night-before bag

archetypes.name: Luggage tags and key cards
archetypes.clicks: A numbered or itemised list is a staple travel pin format ('10 traveler secrets to packing smart' style teasers, per Social Media Today's best-practices piece; list posts perform well per Simple Pin Media). Hanging each item on its own tag makes the list scannable at thumbnail size and turns a plain list into a travel object; one idea per pin (Houfy) with the items as the payoff.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Headline top-left 64-330. A horizontal rail or a suitcase handle across y=400; 3-11 tags hang from it on strings of different lengths, staggered in two rows if more than 6, each tag 200-280px wide with one real item written on it (tag number optional, only if the source list is ordered). For hotel topics the tags become key cards fanned out of a sleeve. Sub line at 1200-1320, product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: luggage-tag x N tied to a suitcase handle or a passport, or hotel-key-card fan with a service-desk-bell.
archetypes.text: One real item per tag, copied verbatim from the product's data (list labels, preparation categories, playbook choices) or the guide's list; heading from the source list if it has one.
archetypes.bestFor: pins whose content is a short set of named options or steps: kinds of trip, kinds of to-do, what was lost, three things to write down, who is on a booking, hotel search order

archetypes.name: Paper in hand (printable mockup)
archetypes.clicks: Printable-mockup pins are how planner and travel-binder printables are sold on Pinterest: the buyer sees the page they will hold (planner sellers' listings and pin template packs all lead with the printed page). Paper backups are a recurring travel-binder theme ('technology can fail when traveling', Savor and Savvy). It also shows the product's real printables, which no competitor pin can.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Headline top 64-300. 300-1250: a printed-sheet, trip-book, clipboard, index card or postcard at a slight 2-4 degree tilt, occupying ~75% width, shown big enough that its rows are legible at phone size (min 26px text); a supporting prop overlaps one corner (pen, phone-low-battery, passport edge, sticky-note). Optional real screenshot in a phone frame overlapping the lower left, max 30% of width. Sub 1260-1360, product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: the product's own printed outputs drawn as paper: the packing list PDF, My Trip Book with its section tabs, the one-page trip card, the trip record; or a handwritten index card or postcard carrying the Companion's authored wording.
archetypes.text: Sheet titles and section names copied from src/products/travel-companion/printables (BOOK_TITLE, SECTION_LIST, tripCard.tsx labels, packing.tsx) and rows from the product data or guide; wording on cards copied from the playbooks' suggestedWording.
archetypes.bestFor: printables, what to keep on paper, packing list PDF, scripts/opening lines, let somebody know, trip record

archetypes.name: Passport and documents flat-lay
archetypes.clicks: Travel document checklists and travel binders/organisers are an established Pinterest category (travel binder printables with document sections; passport-and-documents flat-lays are a standard travel stock composition). The passport is the single most recognisable 'international travel' object, so the pin is read as a documents checklist instantly.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Headline top 64-300. 320-1220: an open travel-folder seen from above, passport(s) open or closed, wallet, envelopes, insurance card, each document carrying a small kraft label card with its real 'whose / where kept' line, aligned to a loose grid; index tabs on the folder carry the real document types. Sub 1240-1340, product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: travel-folder, passport, envelope-confirmation, wallet-and-cards, sticky-note tabs, optionally phone-with-screen of the Trip documents list.
archetypes.text: Document types from DOCUMENT_TYPES (printables/bookContent.ts) or DocumentForm.tsx KIND_OPTIONS; 'where kept' lines from the guide's example table or the real screenshot.
archetypes.bestFor: travel document checklist, where it is kept, lost passport/wallet/phone, first international trip timeline, confirmation numbers

archetypes.name: Departure board
archetypes.clicks: Ordered, time-stamped steps are the format of 'what to do if your flight is delayed' advice (step-by-step guides from airlines, banks and travel sites dominate this query), and itinerary graphics are one of the recommended travel pin types (AdvertiseMint/Social Media Today). A split-flap board is the instantly-recognised airport sign, so a schedule or ordered list reads as 'travel' before a word is read.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Headline top 64-300 on the page colour (not on the board). 330-1250: the dark departure-board panel full width minus 40px margins, a header row of real column labels, 4-9 rows of split-flap text (max ~28 characters per cell row, so long lines are cut to their first clause using the source's own words); an optional status column. Sub 1270-1360 below the board, product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: departure-board with split-flap rows; clock-face top-left of the panel; for time zones, a row of clock-faces above the board.
archetypes.text: Rows copied from guide tables/timelines (times, steps, references) or product data (playbook titles, timezone table, Today labels). Column labels only from the source table's own column names.
archetypes.bestFor: flight delay first steps, itinerary with references, night-before timing, time zones, 'what happens tomorrow', the nine situations

archetypes.name: Boarding pass
archetypes.clicks: Boarding-pass graphics are a widely used travel design device (invitations, trip reveals, giveaways; Morphic, Hongkiat) because the format already means 'trip'. The structured label/value grid also improves readability of a small amount of information, and the tear-off stub gives a natural second hierarchy for a checklist or choice set.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Headline top 64-320. One large boarding pass rotated 90 degrees to run vertically (pass body 330-1180, stub 1180-1330 below a perforation), or 2-4 passes stacked with offsets. Main body: up to 4 label/value pairs in small caps labels + bold values; stub: the choice set or short checklist with tick boxes. Barcode as decoration only. Sub 1340-1400, product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: boarding-pass (single, stacked, or the back of a pass with pen notes), a passport edge or phone-with-screen tucked under it.
archetypes.text: Labels and values are real: playbook prompts and choices (flightProblem.ts), trip card labels (tripCard.tsx), the guide's own booking table, or values from the real screenshots. No invented flight numbers, gates, seats, airport codes or times.
archetypes.bestFor: flight problem choices, notes for the desk, who booked what, the one-page trip card, one-way trips

archetypes.name: Route map
archetypes.clicks: Map and itinerary graphics are core travel-pin imagery and the multi-stop/itinerary pins are what Pinterest travellers use to 'map out their itineraries' (Skift). A dotted route with pins is the shorthand for a trip; using it to show what depends on what makes the product's one unique idea (the change-impact walk) visible in a single glance.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Headline top 64-300. 320-1250: map ground full bleed; 2-4 location pins along a dashed arc or road-route from top-left to bottom-right; each pin has a booking card (kind label + title + time/reference) offset to the open side; dependency arrows between cards where the source says one booking is built on another. Sub 1270-1360 on a solid band, product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: route-map or road-route with location pins, dependency-chain cards, clock-faces for time-zone pins, phone-with-screen for the Today pin.
archetypes.text: Stop names, times and references from the guides' worked examples (multi-stop, flight-changed, one-page itinerary, road trip) or the real screenshots; zone names from TIMEZONE_PLACES.
archetypes.bestFor: multi-stop trips, flight moved and what else it affects, time zones, who to tell, road trip days, Today shows where you are
